| **Summary** | No Mind & Language-specific AI policy page found; journal follows Wiley's publisher-wide generative AI policy (applies platform-wide, not confirmed as customized for this journal). Wiley policy: generative AI/LLM tools cannot be listed as author or co-author; any use of generative AI in developing manuscript content must be disclosed transparently (in Methods, a dedicated disclosure, or Acknowledgements); authors remain fully accountable for all content; AI must not replace human expertise/authorship. This is permissive-with-disclosure (not a ban), hence leniency 3. |
| **Source URL** | https://authors.wiley.com/editors/journal-editors/publication-ethics/generative-ai-fair-use-policy.html |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Interdisciplinary philosophy-of-mind / cognitive-science journal spanning philosophy, linguistics, psychology, AI, cognitive anthropology and cognitive archaeology. Recent Early View / 2025-2026 issues (per Wiley TOC search results) include: theory of mind and other cognitive abilities (special editorial series), the evolutionary psychology of syntax (Tomasello), metacognitive feelings and dreaming, error detection and representation, and — notably — a March 2026 Early View piece on whether structural correspondences can ground real-world representational content in large language models, showing the journal is actively publishing philosophy-of-AI/LLM-representation work alongside classic philosophy-of-mind and psycholinguistics topics.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Analytic philosophical argumentation/theory papers, Empirical cognitive-science and psycholinguistics studies, Philosophy-of-AI / LLM representation and cognition papers, Evolutionary/comparative cognition papers, Interdisciplinary papers bridging linguistics, philosophy, psychology and AI
